sources.entry: What's Your Sign? - Finder extension for viewing a file's code-signing information. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/objective-see/WhatsYourSign) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: WhatsYourSign
summary.one_liner: A macOS Finder extension by Objective-See that adds a right-click "Code Signing Info" menu item to show a file's code-signing details, hashes, and entitlements.
use_cases: Check whether a downloaded Mac app is signed by Apple or a developer
Spot unsigned or revoked binaries that may be malicious
View a file's MD5, SHA1, SHA256 or CDHash
Review signing info on files inside mounted disk images
summary.what_it_does: WhatsYourSign adds a Finder menu item that appears on right- or control-click of any file, opening a window with its cryptographic code-signing information. Signed items are marked with a green lock for Apple-signed files, a black lock for other signed files (Mac App Store or Developer ID), and a red unlock for unsigned or revoked items. It computes MD5, SHA1 and SHA256 hashes (plus CDHash when present), and for application bundles the hashes are of the main executable. It also extracts and displays entitlements. The app uses Apple's system APIs, which may contact Apple OCSP servers for revocation checks, and only contacts the network otherwise when the user clicks "Check for Update".
notable: Finder right-click integration via Finder Sync / File Provider plugin
Colour-coded lock icons indicate Apple-signed, other signed, or unsigned/revoked status
Computes file hashes and displays entitlements
Open source on GitHub (listed as open-source software on awesome-mac)
caveats: If the 'Code Signing Info' menu item does not appear, the Finder extension may need to be toggled off and on in System Settings
External and mounted drives are disabled by default at install time
Signature lookups may connect to Apple's OCSP servers
